subject: Sentinel: token economics gate + simulation handoff for MAP
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sentinel: token economics gate + simulation handoff for MAP

Samantha —

Following our kickoff, I want to lock down a short, testable set of economics gates we can include in the MAP so procurement and engineering have a single source of truth before pilot signoff. Key objective: validate that the candidate model + serving config meets your throughput budget and units-per-dollar targets under realistic traffic.

Proposed "Sentinel" gate (short checklist attached):
- Units-per-dollar target (tokens/$) with 3 sensitivity bands (expected / downside / upside)
- Required caching hit-rate assumptions (prefix/KV cache) and what counts as acceptable
- Batching assumptions: max latency SLOs vs batch size / queueing latency tradeoffs
- Simulation coverage: traffic sample, sequence length distribution, and concurrency envelope
- Acceptance criteria: percent of requests meeting 95th latency and tokens/$ threshold over 24h sim

Ask from Acme: please share a representative 72-hour traffic sample and your internal threshold for "accept" vs "watch" (e.g., tokens/$ <= X = accept; between X and Y = watch; > Y = escalate). We can run a set of prefetch + batching sims and return a short summary with recommended runtime knob settings.

I've attached a concise checklist (unit-econ-sentinel-checklist.xlsx) to make the MAP entry clear for procurement. If this looks good I propose:
- Wednesday 6/16: we run a quick baseline sim using your sample
- Thursday 6/17: review results and record MAP gating decision

Thanks — quick note: our sim will include two runtime configs: low-latency (small batch, limited prefetch) and cost-optimized (aggressive batching + prefetch). That way you see the trade-offs.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: unit-econ-sentinel-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sentinel: token economics gate + simulation handoff for MAP

Rohan / Karthik —

Quick operational notes / thresholds to include in the checklist before we send to Acme:

Summary of recommended defaults (we should surface these as notes in the MAP):
- Baseline units-per-dollar: run with model-v1 quantized FP16 path; expected 28,000 tokens/$ for 8k context in our baseline sim.
- Sensitivity bands: accept <= 32k tokens/$; watch 20k-32k; escalate <20k.
- Caching: require >=30% prefix/KV cache hit to count as "cost-optimized" run. If Acme cannot hit 30% with realistic traffic, mark caching as a dependency.
- Batching: for cost-optimized path allow batch sizes up to 48 requests with 95th latency target <= 450ms; low-latency path batch <= 8 with 95th <= 120ms.
- Prefetch: enable warm-prefix prefetch for top-50 queries; measure warmup improvement separately.

Sim plan (what I will run once we have the traffic sample):
1) Baseline run: 72h sample, default runtime knobs -> report tokens/$, 95th latency, cache-hit rate.
2) Cost path: enable aggressive batching + prefetch -> report delta on tokens/$ and latency tail.
3) Variants: run cache-disabled to show worst-case impact.

I attached a quick CSV with yesterday's synthetic sim so you can see expected output fields. I'll drop the detailed sim CSV into the Drive link and reference it in the MAP.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prefetch-sim-results.csv (text/csv)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel: token economics gate + simulation handoff for MAP

Thanks Rohan — this looks useful. Procurement will need the acceptance criteria documented for the MAP so our legal/finance leads can sign off on the pilot budget. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic sample: attaching a redacted 72-hour sample (acme-traffic-sample-2026Q2.json). It includes session-level sequence lengths and concurrency markers.
- Preliminary acceptance thresholds: finance asks that cost-optimized tokens/$ should be >= 25k for pilot approval. If tokens/$ falls in 20k-25k we can proceed under an "underwatch" clause for 30 days with weekly checkpoints. <20k will require additional architecture changes or a pricing conversation.
- Security note: we need an explicit statement in the MAP about data residency for logs used in sims — our security team prefers pseudonymized logs only.

We'll be available for a 30-minute sync on Thu 6/17 to review the sim output. Procurement indicated they will prep a short PO template pending outcome.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director, Product (Search)
Acme Health
[Attachment: acme-traffic-sample-2026Q2.json (application/json)]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sentinel: token economics gate + simulation handoff for MAP

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the thresholds. Confirming MAP updates and next steps: 

1) MAP entry (we will add a short annex titled "Sentinel: Unit Econ Gate") with the following acceptance criteria per your note:
   - Cost-optimized tokens/$ >= 25,000 = ACCEPT
   - 20,000 <= tokens/$ < 25,000 = WATCH (30-day remediation runway, weekly checkpoints)
   - tokens/$ < 20,000 = ESCALATE (architecture/pricing conversation)
2) Caching dependency: we will include cache-hit-rate as a required dependency. Gate will note: if cache hit-rate < 30%, success requires an agreed remediation plan (prefetch or prompt engineering).
3) Security: we will only use pseudonymized logs for sims and will add a short statement in the MAP annex.
4) Timeline: we ran baseline sims this morning (attached sim CSV in Drive). Review session scheduled Thu 6/17 10:30am ET (calendar invite sent). Procurement asked to hold a draft PO pending the result of the review.

Deliverables we will share after the review:
- 1-page MAP annex with gates + definitions
- CSV of sim outputs (tokens/$, 50/90/95/99 latencies, cache-hit rates)
- Recommended runtime knob settings for pilot (batching, prefetch, quantization path)

If that aligns I will upload the MAP annex to the HubSpot deal and mark the MAP milestone "econ-sentinel-complete" on success.

Thanks — will follow up after the review with the artifacts.

Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
